data.title: Ryuk Labs — positioning
data.body:
# Ryuk Labs — positioning

*From the team outreach master context, updated 2026-10-01 (§3).*

Ryuk Labs is a Dubai-based product design, engineering and applied-AI team. We work alongside founders and operators to understand a real business problem, define the useful product or workflow, build it, and help the team adopt and maintain it.

## What we can contribute
- Product and workflow research
- Product definition and technical direction
- UX and interface design
- Web and mobile engineering
- System integrations and data models
- Applied AI with human review
- Booking, commerce and customer-operation workflows
- Internal operations, ownership and follow-up systems
- Migration, staff training and rollout
- Early demonstrations, adoption and GTM support where agreed

## The strongest commercial framing
Start with one operating problem, not a list of services. Examples:
- Enquiries arrive through disconnected channels and lose ownership.
- Bookings, products, stock and customer records are managed separately.
- A promising prototype needs a maintainable product and operating workflow.
- A founder needs senior technical direction before building a full team.
- A regulated money flow needs a usable customer experience and reliable reconciliation.
- Useful AI output remains inside individual chats instead of becoming team work.

For UAE businesses, make adoption practical: existing WhatsApp and social channels, English and Arabic, migration, team ownership and employee training. Scope, integrations, access, pricing and commercial terms are agreed per engagement.

## Partnership shapes
| Shape | What the other side brings | What Ryuk Labs brings | First step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Client project | A defined workflow, business owner and access to users | Research, product, design, engineering and delivery | Scope one paid pilot |
| Founder/domain partnership | Domain knowledge, customer access and decision time | Technical direction and product delivery | Validate one problem together |
| Referral/commercial partner | Relevant relationships and qualified opportunities | Senior delivery capability | Compare one live opportunity |
| Joint delivery | Complementary capability and a named owner | Product/engineering/AI capacity | Agree responsibilities on one project |
| Venture or portfolio support | Founders with blocked product or AI work | Clinics followed by separately scoped delivery | Support one company first |
| Ecosystem/programme | Community, programme access or a stage | A practical clinic, workshop or pilot format | Run one useful session |

Do not offer fixed equity, free builds, prices or delivery timelines without a specific decision.

data.title: Outreach — lanes, method and voice
data.body:
# Outreach — lanes, method and voice

*From the team outreach master context, updated 2026-10-01 (§4, §13, §16, §18).*

## Keep the four outreach lanes separate
| Lane | Lead with | Suitable proof | Ask |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ryuk Labs partnership/client work | A real product, workflow or delivery gap | One relevant Ryuk Labs story | One project discussion, joint-delivery fit or introduction |
| Personal technical-founder support | Ryuk's hands-on technical direction and founder empathy | Personal building experience | A short conversation about the founder's actual problem |
| Sharingu company-building | The contribution thesis, early use and distribution need | Current Sharingu traction | A walkthrough |
| Sharingu pilot | One recurring handoff between people and agents | A concrete handoff example | A scoped pilot with a small team and agreed measures |

Never combine Ryuk Labs services, Sharingu, Siru country expansion and an event-pass request in one opener.

*The investment side of the Sharingu lanes is left out of sharingu's data (fundraising stays in the team context pack).* The relationship goal is mutual value: we are not collecting senior profiles or sending the same sales message to everyone.

## Method
Before writing: choose one lane and outcome; check relationship state; verify current role and a relevant detail; map the mandate to one capability and one proof point; choose one small ask.

Contact ladder: follow a reachable operator; interact around a concrete theme; connect; send one relevant idea; ask for a short perspective call after a response; ask who owns pilots/partnerships if fit is real; approach senior leadership with context.

Operational rule: no more than five new DMs in a day. Contact one primary person per organization. Follow up once after roughly 6–8 business days with a useful detail or artifact. Stop after a decline or opt-out.

## Voice
Write like a thoughtful builder: short sentences, plain language, one purpose, one reason, one proof point and one easy next step.

Avoid "hope this email finds you well", "revolutionary", "game-changing", "seamless ecosystem", "unlock synergies", "leverage", inflated praise, manufactured urgency and fake familiarity. Do not mention a recipient's post unless it genuinely adds something and was actually reviewed; a direct relevant opening is better. The first DM does not need a question.

Editorial targets: connection note under 200 characters where possible; first DM 45–80 words; first email 100–150 words; replies answer the recipient's question first.

## What stays unknown
Do not guess legal entity details, licence/registration data, incorporation, address, jurisdiction, cap table, equity, valuation, instrument, runway, current revenue/ARR, transaction volume, paying-customer count, employee breakdown, the exact definition of Siru's sign-ups, Sharingu retention/activity, unapproved client identities, exact integrations, or event outcomes.

## Privacy and operating rule
Do not publish raw transcripts, confidential client identities, production credentials, old invoices, form-response data or internal operational records. The team may draft, research and update internal status from evidence. Do not send messages, submit forms, schedule follow-ups, post content or change a contact to "sent" without a real action or explicit confirmation. A draft is not evidence of a send, a connection is not a reply, and a reply is not a meeting.

data.title: Campaigns and angles
data.body:
# Campaigns and angles

*From the team outreach master context, updated 2026-10-01 (§1, §7). Relationship state and named contacts are kept out of sharingu.*

The commercial objective: turn Ryuk Labs' product, engineering and applied-AI capability into real projects, delivery partnerships, referrals and ecosystem relationships, with the UAE and UK as the main markets.

## A. Event access, stages and partner activations
The best hook is not "please give me a free pass." Offer a format that creates audience value:
1. **Live founder clinic:** one real business problem becomes the smallest testable product or AI workflow in 25 minutes.
2. **Human–agent handoff session:** show why completed AI output can still fail the next teammate, and how evidence, ownership and goals travel with the work.
3. **Cross-border product panel:** the difference between exporting software and adapting workflows for India, UAE and UK markets.
4. **Physical experience + digital layer:** Ryuk Labs and TakeOver IRL on technology, community and real-world founder experiences.
5. **Pharmacy digitisation discussion:** what must change beyond code when localising a live Indian pharmacy product to another country.

Ask in this order: useful format → correct programme/partnership owner → stage, roundtable or partner activation → access/pass needed to contribute. A pass is the outcome, not the headline. A normal pass is still a win; a VIP pass is not the opening ask. The selected events are on the Targets list.

## B. UAE and UK business development
The strongest offer is founder-led product execution for one real opportunity, not generic outsourced development. Target venture value-creation teams, startup studios, implementation partners, innovation programmes, cross-border networks and enterprises with a named workflow. The routes are on the Targets list.

## C. Siru country customisation
Do not pitch "copy Siru into another country." Pitch a repeatable product core plus country discovery across regulation, pharmacy workflow, payments/providers, language, integrations, migration, staff adoption, training, commercial ownership and distribution. The initial conversation should be market learning, operator feedback or a scoped discovery partnership. Pharmacy platforms may be partners, channels or competitors; do not disclose proprietary architecture or customer data.

## D. Fintech, crypto and neobank projects
Relevant themes: wallet funding, card payment and reconciliation; onboarding; ledger and operational workflows; embedded-finance and SME banking experiences; stablecoin payment workflows; internal compliance/review systems; product engineering for regulated digital-asset businesses. Never imply Ryuk Labs is itself a licensed bank, payment provider, broker, exchange or crypto custodian.

## E. Real estate and hospitality
The useful angle is AI-assisted operations: enquiry intake from WhatsApp, portals and social channels; property/guest/tenant context; booking, viewing and service-request ownership; staff handoffs; multilingual operations; and management visibility without replacing working systems. Keep messages grounded in one operating workflow.

data.title: Content strategy
data.body:
# Content strategy

*From the team outreach master context, updated 2026-10-01 (§12, §15).*

Publish two useful posts per week: one operating/product lesson and one founder or cross-border lesson. Leave three to five substantial comments per week; add an example, counterpoint or practical implication, never only "great insights."

Weekly rhythm: two evidence-led posts; three to five meaningful comments; one existing-conversation review before new outreach; one weekly status reconciliation using actual send/reply evidence.

## Post themes
1. **Siru localisation** — "A pharmacy platform is not ready for a new country because its code runs there." Explain regulation, workflow, payments/providers, language, migration/integration and staff adoption; invite pharmacy operators in the UAE or UK to challenge the model.
2. **Sharingu handoff** — "AI can complete a task and still leave the company with more confusion." Show one before/after handoff: goal, affected screens/APIs, evidence, owner and next action. Avoid a feature catalogue.
3. **The partner contract** — "The best product partnerships start with a shared problem and clear responsibility on both sides." What the domain partner brings and what Ryuk Labs contributes; useful for studios, consultancies and portfolio value-creation teams.
4. **Cross-border field note** — "Entering the UAE or UK is a workflow-discovery exercise before it is a translation exercise." One concrete operational contrast between India, UAE and UK; ask operators for the local constraint outsiders usually miss.
5. **Fintech operations** — "The payment screen is the visible part. Reconciliation, ownership and exception handling decide whether the product works operationally." Use an anonymous workflow example; do not imply client identity, transaction volume or licensing.

data.question: May the named public stories (Siru, FlowZo, Redacted/TOKEN2049) be filed as approved claims on the GTM tab?
data.why: The team context pack approves a description and an exact boundary for each (§5), and each is a public story on ryuklabs.io; but each names a client or partner, and this fill files no client names without the owner's say. Option A is the recommendation: they are public, and the boundaries (e.g. "keep the number as 10,000+ sign-ups until the unit is confirmed"; "1M+ means owner-reported registrations/applications") are exactly what a teammate needs before writing copy.

options.what: Yes: file the three as approved claims, each with its boundary and story link
options.tradeoff: Team context pack §5; the stories are public on ryuklabs.io/stories. The names enter the org's data on Cloudflare.
